scope: Read-only source and installed SDK review; no calibration, training, GPU, VM, model, build, install or network execution.

routes.implementedBehavior: Creates exact3B model from initialization seed, materializes GPU parameters, measures forward/backward/AdamW update on deterministic random inputs and records finite loss/changed weights. It is a bounded training-mechanics allocation probe, not a saved model inference or a guest GPU benchmark.
routes.measurement: ContinuousClock starts before model construction and ends after evaluation and finite-logit validation. mechanicsActiveElapsedSeconds includes CPU orchestration, model allocation, evaluation, training, synchronization and validation; not GPU-only duration.
routes.reuseNow: Do not invoke. Reuse distinctions between unavailable versus measured observations; retain actual device identity and explicit timing scope.

routes.limit: Coordinates cooperating processes that use the same resource root. Does not reserve hardware against window compositor, other apps or a process using another lock path, and does not create a GPU virtual device.

routes.implementedBehavior: PGDeviceDescriptor selects host MTLDevice and requires guest memory/task mapping, read and interrupt callbacks; PGDevice exposes MMIO/display/suspend/resume/stop. PGDeviceSpec declares PCI BAR MMIO16KiB, MSI and Apple vendor/device IDs.
routes.limit: A host Metal HVC callback alone is not this Apple virtual PCI device. No need to construct PGDevice for the narrow typed geometry offload experiment.

routes.implementedBehavior: Immutable ARM guest sends typed geometry request through HVC; host validates request, executes real Metal compute, returns finite F32 vector result for guest readback.
routes.name: custom guest-controlled GPU offload service
routes.limit: Not Apple PGDevice, guest-native Metal driver, GPU scheduling isolation, learned model output, automatic model derivation of hardware or guest OS boot.

measurementRequirements.requirement: Require command-buffer status completed and error nil before accepting output. GPUStartTime is zero before execution; GPUEndTime is zero before completion notification, per installed header lines286–294.

Preserve both raw GPU timestamps; use finite positive start/end and end>=start. Missing, zero, NaN, infinity or reversed values are unavailable/invalid timing, never substitute host elapsed or invent duration. A zero difference cannot support throughput or speedup division.

GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime are host seconds. Use their difference together. Keep ContinuousClock or DispatchTime interval measurements separate; do not subtract a raw mach tick or guest counter from Metal host seconds. Raw sampleTimestamps counters would require explicit timebase calibration.

Record pipeline/device/queue creation separately. Retain cold first dispatch, then explicit equal warmup counts per tested route; exclude only predeclared warmups and preserve them. Both routes should reuse the same compiled kernel/device and inputs. Alternate paired route order or report fixed-order/cache bias.

Report caller total wall, VM creation/map/register setup, guest entry/HVC transition, host callback wall, Metal command execution interval, readback/validation and cleanup as distinct scoped values where measured. Do not label total guest route minus GPU interval as exact vCPU-only overhead.

Shared buffers require completed GPU execution before CPU read. If changed to managed/private storage, use appropriate explicit synchronization/copy and include its cost in the declared interval. Validate all returned vector elements and unchanged request/code guards.

A 200-point/12-node field workload may be overhead dominated. Record point/node counts, repeat counts and individual samples; do not infer GPU utilization, TFLOPS or acceleration for model workloads from this tiny dispatch.

Record actual MTLDevice name/registryID/unified memory. Serial bounded own work avoids self-contention but advisory leases do not remove other OS GPU work. Timing variation alone is not a virtualization defect.

On each evaluation clear prior timing/status/error fields before validation, or attach them only to a successful current command. Invalid input must not inherit a preceding successful dispatch timestamp. CPU formula is an independent comparison, never a silent fallback.
GPU/CPU numeric parity validates field computation; host/guest byte parity validates offload transport. Neither changes historical model authority nor trains weights.
